body:
_Migrated from issue #1202, filed 2026-07-28._

## What happened

#1201 took the Docker integration suite down to `37 passed, 80 errors` — every error at fixture setup, so the suite exercised almost nothing. The workflow still reported **success**, and it stayed that way long enough that the breakage was found by reading a log rather than by a red check.

## Why

`Integration Tests (Docker)` is `continue-on-error` outside `safe-tier-2` PRs, and `test-summary` treats any integration result other than a tier-2 failure as advisory:

```yaml
if [[ "${{ needs.integration-tests.result }}" == "failure" ]]; then
  if [[ "$IS_TIER2_PR" == "true" ]]; then
    echo "❌ Integration tests failed on safe-tier-2 PR — auto-merge gate"
    exit 1
  fi
  echo "⚠️ Integration tests failed (advisory; not a tier-2 PR)"
fi
```

Advisory-on-main is a deliberate, documented choice (the job is slow and its failures shouldn't block auto-revert decisions), and this issue is not asking to reverse it.

The gap is that the summary cannot tell **"a few tests failed"** from **"the suite could not run at all."** Those are different classes. The first is noise you reasonably ride out; the second means the gate is dark and every subsequent green is meaningless — including the hard gate on tier-2 PRs, which in this case couldn't pass at all.

## Suggested shape

Have the integration job surface a machine-readable outcome (it already writes `integration-results.xml`) and have `test-summary` treat *mass setup/collection errors* — say, errors greatly outnumbering passes, or zero tests actually executing — as a hard failure regardless of tier, while leaving ordinary test failures advisory as they are today.

#1201 moves detection of its specific cause into Fast Tests, which is a hard gate, so that particular breakage cannot silently recur. This issue is about the general case: any future reason the suite goes dark.

Related: #1105, #953, #1017.
title: CI: an integration suite that cannot run at all still reports the workflow green
